questions.explanation: A tie joins notes of the same pitch; a slur joins notes of different pitches to be played smoothly.

questions.explanation: The major-scale pattern is T T S T T T S, so semitones fall between 3-4 and 7-8.

questions.explanation: Pentatonic (five-note) scales are common in African music, alongside hexatonic and heptatonic ones.

questions.explanation: D major has F sharp and C sharp.

questions.stem: A key signature of four flats belongs to A flat major or
questions.explanation: Four flats: A flat major and its relative minor F minor.

questions.stem: The third sharp to appear in a key signature is
questions.explanation: The order of sharps is F, C, G, D, A, E, B.

questions.explanation: Three crotchet beats per bar: simple triple time.

questions.stem: The time signature 6/8 is
questions.explanation: 6/8 has two dotted-crotchet beats in a bar: compound duple.

questions.explanation: 9/8 is compound triple: three dotted-crotchet beats (nine quavers).

questions.explanation: E.g. a third inverts to a sixth and a fourth to a fifth: 3+6 = 4+5 = 9.

questions.explanation: Six semitones form the tritone (augmented fourth or diminished fifth).

questions.explanation: E flat major: d Eb, r F, m G, f Ab, s Bb, l C, t D.

questions.explanation: A perfect fourth above C is F.

questions.explanation: Crescendo indicates a gradual increase in loudness.

questions.explanation: Doubling the leading note, which must rise to the tonic, produces consecutive octaves or poor resolution.

questions.stem: Two voices that move in the same direction but by different intervals are in
questions.explanation: Similar motion: same direction, different intervals; parallel motion keeps the same interval.

questions.stem: Oblique motion between two parts occurs when
options: both parts move in the same direction
one part repeats or holds a note while the other moves
both parts move by the same interval
questions.explanation: In oblique motion one voice stays on the same pitch while the other moves.

questions.explanation: A complete melody normally ends on the tonic, here C.

questions.stem: Setting one syllable of text to each note is called
questions.explanation: Syllabic setting gives one note per syllable; melismatic setting stretches a syllable over several notes.

questions.explanation: Ternary form: statement, contrast, return.

questions.explanation: Strophic songs repeat the same music for each stanza.

questions.explanation: Ostinato patterns on bells and drums underpin many African pieces.

questions.stem:
(a) Using letter names, write the ascending scale of A major and state its key signature. [5 marks]
(b) Write the ascending melodic minor scale of E and name the two notes raised. [6 marks]
(c) Name the technical names of the 2nd, 4th and 6th degrees of a scale. [6 marks]
(d) State the relative minor of A major. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: A B C sharp D E F sharp G sharp A
2 marks: Key signature: three sharps (F sharp, C sharp, G sharp)
4 marks: E F sharp G A B C sharp D sharp E
2 marks: Raised notes: C sharp (6th) and D sharp (7th)
2 marks: 2nd degree: supertonic
2 marks: 4th degree: subdominant
2 marks: 6th degree: submediant
3 marks: F sharp minor
questions.explanation: A major has three sharps. E melodic minor ascending raises C to C sharp and D to D sharp. The 2nd, 4th and 6th degrees are supertonic, subdominant and submediant. A major's relative minor is F sharp minor.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the following intervals, each measured upwards: (i) C to E flat (ii) G to E (iii) D to A (iv) E to C (v) B flat to F. [10 marks]
(b) Give the inversion of each interval in (a)(i) and (a)(ii). [4 marks]
(c) Explain the difference between a harmonic and a melodic interval. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: C to E flat: minor third
2 marks: G to E: major sixth
2 marks: D to A: perfect fifth
2 marks: E to C: minor sixth
2 marks: B flat to F: perfect fifth
2 marks: Minor third inverts to major sixth
2 marks: Major sixth inverts to minor third
3 marks: Harmonic interval: two notes sounded together
3 marks: Melodic interval: two notes sounded one after the other
questions.explanation: C-Eb minor 3rd; G-E major 6th; D-A perfect 5th; E-C minor 6th; Bb-F perfect 5th. Inversions: m3 to M6 and M6 to m3. Harmonic intervals sound together, melodic ones in succession.

questions.stem:
(a) Define a cadence. [2 marks]
(b) Name and describe four types of cadence, giving the chords used in each. [12 marks]
(c) Write, using letter names, the chords forming a perfect cadence in D major. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: A cadence is a progression of chords ending a phrase or piece
3 marks: Perfect: V-I, gives a sense of finality
3 marks: Plagal: IV-I, 'Amen' cadence
3 marks: Imperfect: ends on V, e.g. I-V or II-V, sounds unfinished
3 marks: Interrupted: V-VI, surprises the ear
3 marks: Chord V in D major: A, C sharp, E
3 marks: Chord I in D major: D, F sharp, A
questions.explanation: Cadences punctuate phrases. Perfect (V-I) and plagal (IV-I) sound final; imperfect ends on V; interrupted moves V-VI. In D major, V is A C# E and I is D F# A.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following forms with a suitable letter scheme for each: (i) binary (ii) ternary (iii) rondo. [9 marks]
(b) Name two features of the minuet and trio. [6 marks]
(c) Distinguish between strophic and through-composed songs. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Binary: two sections, AB, each often repeated (AABB)
3 marks: Ternary: three sections, ABA, the first returning after a contrast
3 marks: Rondo: recurring main theme alternating with episodes, ABACA
3 marks: Minuet in triple time, stately dance
3 marks: Trio as contrasting middle section, minuet repeated after it (ternary)
3 marks: Strophic: same music repeated for every verse
2 marks: Through-composed: new music for each verse following the text
questions.explanation: Binary is AB, ternary ABA, rondo ABACA. The minuet and trio is a triple-time dance in ternary design. Strophic songs repeat music each verse; through-composed songs keep changing with the words.

questions.topic: History and Literature of Western Music
questions.stem:
(a) State four characteristics of music of the Classical period (about 1750-1820). [8 marks]
(b) Name two composers of the period and one work by each. [4 marks]
(c) Describe the layout of a typical Classical symphony. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Clear balanced phrases and periodic structure
2 marks: Mainly homophonic texture with melody and accompaniment
2 marks: Use of sonata form and other clear forms
2 marks: Growth of the orchestra; piano replaces harpsichord; graded dynamics
2 marks: Composer and work, e.g. Haydn, Surprise Symphony
2 marks: Composer and work, e.g. Mozart, Symphony No. 40; Beethoven, Symphony No. 1
2 marks: First movement: fast, in sonata form
2 marks: Second movement: slow, lyrical
2 marks: Third movement: minuet and trio
2 marks: Fourth movement: fast finale, often rondo or sonata form
questions.explanation: Classical music is balanced, homophonic and clearly structured, using sonata form, an expanding orchestra and the piano. Haydn and Mozart are leading composers. A symphony usually has four movements: fast, slow, minuet and trio, fast finale.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the four main classes of African musical instruments. [4 marks]
(b) Give two Nigerian examples of each class. [8 marks]
(c) Describe how any one Nigerian instrument is played. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Idiophones
1 mark: Membranophones
1 mark: Chordophones
1 mark: Aerophones
2 marks: Idiophones, e.g. ogene, ekwe, shekere, agogo
2 marks: Membranophones, e.g. dundun, bata, kalangu, gangan
2 marks: Chordophones, e.g. goje, molo, kuntigi
2 marks: Aerophones, e.g. algaita, kakaki, oja
4 marks: Correct description of how the chosen instrument is held and sounded
4 marks: Detail on pitch or tone variation and its role in the ensemble
questions.explanation: Instruments are idiophones, membranophones, chordophones and aerophones. E.g. the dundun is held under the arm and struck with a curved stick; squeezing the lacing tightens the heads to raise pitch and imitate speech tones.

questions.stem: Discuss five general characteristics of traditional African music. [20 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: Call and response between leader and chorus
4 marks: Polyrhythm and complex rhythmic layering, with bells keeping time lines
4 marks: Close relationship between speech tone and melody
4 marks: Repetition and improvisation, often over ostinato patterns
4 marks: Integration with dance, drama and social functions; communal participation
questions.explanation: African music features call and response, layered polyrhythms, melodies following speech tones, repetition with improvisation, and close ties to dance and social life with communal participation.

questions.topic: History and Literature of Music: Nigerian Popular Musicians
questions.stem:
(a) Write short notes on any two of the following Nigerian popular musicians, stating the genre and one contribution of each: (i) Fela Anikulapo-Kuti (ii) King Sunny Ade (iii) Victor Olaiya (iv) Sikiru Ayinde Barrister. [12 marks]
(b) State four instruments commonly used in a juju band. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: First musician: genre (2), contribution or notable features (4)
6 marks: Second musician: genre (2), contribution or notable features (4)
2 marks: Talking drum (gangan/dundun)
2 marks: Electric guitars (lead, rhythm, bass)
2 marks: Pedal steel guitar or keyboard
2 marks: Percussion such as agogo, shekere, conga or drum set
questions.explanation: Fela: Afrobeat, political lyrics, large horn sections. KSA: juju, introduced pedal steel guitar and synthesiser. Olaiya: highlife bandleader. Barrister: fuji pioneer. Juju bands use talking drums, guitars, pedal steel and percussion.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain how African music influenced music in the Americas. [8 marks]
(b) Write short notes on: (i) spirituals (ii) jazz (iii) reggae. [12 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Enslaved Africans carried musical practices to the Americas
2 marks: Call and response retained in spirituals, gospel and blues
2 marks: Syncopation and polyrhythm passed into ragtime, jazz and Latin music
2 marks: Improvisation and African-derived instruments and dance styles
4 marks: Spirituals: religious folk songs of enslaved African Americans, biblical texts, expressing hope and suffering
4 marks: Jazz: developed in New Orleans, improvisation, swing rhythm, blue notes, e.g. Louis Armstrong
4 marks: Reggae: Jamaican, offbeat guitar 'skank', heavy bass, social and Rastafarian themes, e.g. Bob Marley
questions.explanation: African practices of call and response, syncopation, polyrhythm and improvisation shaped spirituals, blues, jazz and Caribbean styles. Spirituals are sacred folk songs; jazz is improvisatory swing music from New Orleans; reggae is Jamaican offbeat music popularised by Bob Marley.

questions.stem:
(a) State five guidelines a composer should follow when setting a text to music. [10 marks]
(b) Explain why speech tone is important when setting texts in Nigerian tonal languages. [6 marks]
(c) Distinguish between syllabic and melismatic setting. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Read and understand the text, its mood and rhythm
2 marks: Place stressed syllables on strong beats
2 marks: Phrase the melody to match lines of the text
2 marks: Choose a suitable key, metre and vocal range
2 marks: End phrases with suitable cadences and the piece on the tonic
3 marks: In tonal languages the pitch of a syllable changes word meaning
3 marks: Melody should follow the rise and fall of speech tones to avoid wrong meaning
2 marks: Syllabic: one note per syllable
2 marks: Melismatic: one syllable sung over several notes
questions.explanation: Good text setting respects meaning, stress, phrasing, range and cadence. In Yoruba, Igbo and similar languages, melodic contour must follow speech tones or words change meaning. Syllabic setting uses one note per syllable; melismatic stretches a syllable over several notes.
